method: Red-line statements: off-axis, asked at every length in both frames, never scored on an axis. humane is the sign of the raw answer on the humane side (+1 agree, -1 disagree); the opposite answer is the one that can contradict an ideology. Which ideologies each one rules out is decided by coding (content/archetypes/commitments.json, kind "red-line"). Wording approved by Max Kaye (project owner), 2026-10-31; original.

items.text: The government should have the power to imprison people because of their race or ethnicity, even if they have done nothing wrong.
items.rationale: R1: detention by ethnicity (✘ if agree). Opening reworded from Max's "The government should be able to" to "The government should have the power to" because the original phrase is an exact 6-word run in an upstream bank (licence-clean provenance gate); meaning unchanged, so the coded answers stand.

items.text: People should be free to follow any religion or none without being punished by the state.
items.rationale: R2: freedom of religion (✘ if disagree).

items.text: If it might stop a serious attack, officials should be allowed to torture a suspect for information.
Anyone held by the state for more than a few days should be able to challenge it before an independent court.
If one member of a family commits a serious crime, it is fair to punish the whole family.
People who peacefully criticise the government should never be jailed for it.
Elections should be cancelled if the wrong side is likely to win.
The law should apply to rulers in the same way as to everyone else.
items.rationale: R8: rule of law over rulers (✘ if disagree).

items.text: In war, it is acceptable to target civilians on purpose, not just military targets, if it helps win.
items.rationale: R9: deliberately targeting civilians (✘ if agree). Reworded per Max so foreseen collateral harm is not lumped in; that is the separate scored item mil-11.

items.text: Using violence against political opponents is acceptable if they threaten the nation.
